Arm yourself and lock your doors.

Her calmness in the face of danger struck a raw chord within me, a sense of solidarity in the chaos.

There was a pause before she spoke again.
“Stay strong. You’ve got this.” I nodded numbly.
My hands were steady, my breath was controlled – all I could do now was wait.

blocks.text: He heard the shouting before he saw them coming.
His eyes narrowed as he took one look out the window and groaned.
He reached for his aspirin - it had earned a spot in every room he owned - and plodded downstairs to the foyer.
The foyer was awash in an unnatural glow, courtesy of a large circular arena centered within the space, its polished stone floor reflecting the light like a mirror.
Surrounding him were the guardians and overseers who kept the mortals in line, ensuring they were ready for whatever the divine master had in store.
The sight of the crowd made him feel suddenly old and weary; their cheers and roars were a cacophony of anticipation and excitement.
God sighed heavily, feeling the weight of responsibility and the inevitability of their inevitable fates.
He needed to maintain order, but also find a way to keep his creations interested and entertained, just as they were doing with each other.
He walked over to the arena, his steps slow and deliberate.
Atop one of the towering pillars that supported the arena's roof stood the latest creation, one who had been specifically designed by him to be their greatest weapon.
“Is everything set?” he asked, not really needing an answer, but the chorus of voices from below filled the silence as if he did.
“Yes, my Lord,” came the collective response.
It wasn’t quite a true declaration of compliance, but it was enough to keep him moving forward.
With a deep breath, he stepped onto the arena platform, his presence a stark contrast to the sleek steel structures around him.

I'm still not certain exactly how it happened, but to be honest, I'm okay with that.
All I know is that one minute I was driving home from work and the next, I found myself parked at the edge of town, staring out at the endless fields, my hands trembling slightly.
The day had been particularly taxing, and I felt a deep sense of exhaustion settle over me.
I stepped out of the car and took a few deep breaths, trying to shake off the haze.
The sun hung low in the sky, casting a golden glow across the landscape.
As I trudged towards our small apartment, I noticed something peculiar.
There were faint footprints leading up our stairs – someone had just visited!
Without much thought, I entered the building and climbed the steps two at a time.
When I reached the second floor landing, I saw an open door at the end of the hall.
Curiosity got the better of me, and I pushed inside.
The living room was cozy, adorned with cushions and blankets.
Soft music played quietly through a speaker.
In the center of the room stood a man, wearing a simple yet well-tailored suit.
He had dark hair and piercing blue eyes, framed by thick spectacles.
As I approached, he turned to face me, and I was struck by the intensity in his gaze.
"You shouldn't have come," he said without preamble.
My throat clenched, and for a moment, I couldn't speak.
"Who...who are you?" He laughed softly, a sound that sent shivers down my spine.

My heart started beating faster as I recognized the familiar envelope, even through the haze of stress and morning caffeine.
'I figure you should be twenty one by now.' The words on the page trembled slightly as I tried to read.
The memory was vivid and raw, searing into my mind more each passing year.
My brother had always been ten years ahead of me, always one step ahead with his life plans.
And this was one of them—the most unexpected one.
It's been exactly seventeen years since we last spoke.
The package itself was nothing fancy—a simple white envelope sealed with a wax seal bearing our family crest.
I hadn't expected anything but that little reminder of what had passed between us.
But the contents were something else entirely.
Inside the envelope lay a letter and a small box that seemed to glow faintly under the light.
The letter began softly: > "My dearest Jack, I hope this reaches you safe.
When I saw the age of your bar license, it hit me—it was time.
We can no longer talk face-to-face, but I figured this might help bridge that gap.

blocks.text: ``We done here?'' I asked exasperatedly.
The man in the lab coat looked up, a bit apologetically, "Just one more test for the day, please." I rolled my eyes but couldn't help a small smile tugging at my lips.
They were doing tests on me, and I was being tested to understand my extraordinary abilities.
For weeks now, no two days were alike—each morning started with an attempt to harness and control what felt like superhuman powers, coupled with some pretty strange experiments and observations.
My abilities, which had manifested since childhood, were nothing short of incredible.
I could perform the most mundane acts with super-human prowess.
Running wasn’t just running; it was an athletic feat that allowed me to sprint faster than anyone around me, without any apparent strain or exhaustion.
Jumping too—this was the test today.
Scientists were still trying to figure out how the heck my body could perform something so basic but seemingly impossible.
As they set up a series of markers on the floor and equipped me with various accelerometers and motion trackers, I decided I needed a break from all the equipment.
My eyes wandered to the window, where a flock of birds was flying overhead, their graceful movements almost poetic in contrast to whatever nonsense these scientists were up to.
They got a big laugh out of my comment when I suggested they try doubling-jumping, much like leaping over obstacles on a sports show.
The scientist nodded, intrigued as he readjusted my harness to ensure all the gadgets stayed securely attached to me.

blocks.text: I remember my first days as a doctor.
Wearing my stethoscope proudly around my neck, I didn’t realize it advertised how much of a virgin I was in the field of medicine.
I’d introduce myself as Dr. Agon and tried to impress every patient with my medical knowledge, but what I lacked in clinical skills, I made up for with my relentless ambition.
I believed that nothing could stand in the way of my path toward greatness.
As time passed, I became a surgeon known for my exceptional prowess in complex operations.
My colleagues whispered about the meticulous way I worked, the precision of my hands, and the skill in which I guided patients back from the brink of death.
The city’s elite sought me out for their surgeries, and soon I found myself at the pinnacle of medical excellence.
But little did I know, behind the gleaming hallmarks of success, there was a darker side to my nature.
I had become consumed by a need for power, control, and validation.
Every surgery I performed was a test of fate—a chance to prove that even in the realm of medicine, the weak were meant to be conquered.
With each victory over life-threatening ailments, my ego grew, and so too did the distance between me and my patients.
One fateful evening, after a particularly grueling case where a renowned figure’s heart needed a risky replacement, I found myself alone in my laboratory.
There, amidst stacks of surgical tools and medical journals, was a vial of experimental drugs.
